chunks: And Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim narrated from ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, from Aḥmad ibn Ismāʿīl al-Kātib, from his father, who said:

Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام came into al-Masjid al-Ḥarām, and some of them said: “If only you would send one of yourselves to ask him.” So a young man from among them came to him and said: “O uncle, what is the greatest of the major sins?”

He said: “Drinking alcohol.” Then he came back to them and informed them. They said to him: “Return to him.” They kept at him until he returned to him and asked him, so he said to him: “Did I not tell you, O son of my brother, [it is] drinking alcohol? Indeed, drinking alcohol causes its companion to enter into adultery, theft, and killing a soul...”
and into shirk with Allah. And the effects of alcohol rise above every sin, just as its tree rises above every tree.”

key_terms.السَّرِقَةِ: theft; unlawful taking of another’s property
key_terms.الشِّرْكِ بِاللَّهِ: associating partners with Allah; the gravest theological sin
key_terms.الْكَبَائِرِ: the major sins; grave acts for which severe divine punishment is threatened
key_terms.شُرْبُ الْخَمْرِ: drinking alcohol; presented here as the gravest of major sins because it leads to many others
key_terms.قَتْلِ النَّفْسِ: killing a soul; unlawful taking of life

ai.seo_question: Why is drinking alcohol described as one of the greatest major sins in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith relates that Imam Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Bāqir عليه السلام identified drinking alcohol as the greatest of the major sins. He explains that it leads a person into other grave sins such as adultery, theft, murder, and shirk, highlighting its corrupting and far-reaching moral consequences.
